claim: Pep4Fish reported on 19 October that AgroGrINTech had started a pilot unit in Pedrouços, Maia.
The AgroGrINTech unit can produce about 200kg of bromelain a year from about 120 tonnes of pineapple by-products.
The planned 2025 production capacity was 50kg of bromelain, and the unit's capacity is four times that.
Investment in the unit comes to about 1.2 million euros by the end of 2026, from Portugal's Recovery and Resilience Plan and private money.
AICEP Portugal Global reported on 4 November on the aims of the Pep4Fish project.
The ETSA Group leads the Pep4Fish project with nine partners.
Débora Campos is the CEO and founder of AgroGrINTech.
The Portuguese Catholic University's Centre for Biotechnology and Fine Chemistry research underlying the process was licensed exclusively to AgroGrINTech in 2025.
AgroGrINTech aims to sign its first supply contracts in 2027 and plans to open an investment round early in 2027.
Seamoretech is a 2021 spin-off of the University of Porto's Faculty of Engineering and plans to launch in Spain in 2027.
